correctness.rationale: The six-clause closed \(\mathrm{FO}^{4}\) sentence defines an intrinsic two-class relation via common neighbors; transitivity and the outside-pair axiom force exactly two parts, and common-neighbor uniqueness, minimum degree three and the quadrangle construction give precisely the finite projective-plane incidence axioms. The converse follows from these axioms. For the lower bound, nonempty relative pattern cells for two pebbled vertices in the given symmetric designs produce a permanent Duplicator three-pebble strategy, including Fano and its \(2\)-\((7,4,2)\) complementary biplane. Three separately implemented Python programs check the syntax/semantics, witness graphs and extension patterns; computations do not replace the universal proofs.

value.rationale: The natural complete projective-plane incidence graph family has a sharp finite-variable recognition threshold independent of order and coordinatizability, and the witness proves an exact nontrivial lower bound against all simple graphs. The broad symmetric-design \(\mathrm{FO}^{3}\) collapse gives a structural explanation for why local pebbled patterns cannot recover unique point-line intersections. This is a motivated global boundary in descriptive complexity, not a small parameter lookup.
